title: Production compiler entry promotion
hypothesis: A reusable npm production entry can make the already-supported SceneSpec to immutable BuildPlan to admission-gated native Blender 5.2 compiler chain the preferred auditable release path, while retaining the restricted compiler as a low-level control and preserving B01/B02 plan and canonical structure identities across four fresh production invocations.

frozenObservation.promotionBoundary: A later release step may treat budget report v0.2 child.pid as the production supervisor's native child receipt; orchestration changes require separate preregistration and B01/B02 regression.

requirements: Commit and push this exact spec, protocol and journal entry before creating any production or B56 tool byte, release manifest, package alias or B56 output root.
Commit and push the exact release manifest, five production paths, three B56 tools and package alias change before creating the official preflight root.

The official preflight must start zero Blender processes and create four production preflight records through the preferred npm alias; commit and push accepted evidence before creating attempt or formal roots.
The B56 formal runner is single-use. Preserve every partial output; a repair or rerun requires a new experiment ID.

forbidden: network access during preflight or formal execution except local git reads
mutation, deletion or reuse of B54/B55 evidence
reuse, deletion or mutation of a pre-existing B56 output

requirements: Bind the three exact npm aliases and all production tool hashes.
Bind the unchanged compiler, admission, budget, CompileReceipt, Blender audit and SceneSpec dependencies.
Freeze the attempt/admission/receipt ordering, output layout, disk policy, runtime identities and claim boundary.
Declare compile:restricted as a low-level development/control path, not the preferred auditable release entry.

productionEntryContract.preflightCli: npm run preflight:production -- --scene-spec RELATIVE_JSON --preflight-root RELATIVE_FRESH_DIR --output-root RELATIVE_FRESH_DIR --release-commit FULL_SHA
productionEntryContract.compileCli: npm run compile:production -- --scene-spec RELATIVE_JSON --preflight-root RELATIVE_ACCEPTED_DIR --attempt-root RELATIVE_FRESH_DIR --output-root RELATIVE_FRESH_DIR --preflight-evidence-commit FULL_SHA
preflightRequirements: Resolve every spelling strictly below the real repository root without symbolic-link traversal.
Require the release manifest, package, production tools, unchanged dependencies and SceneSpec to be tracked-clean and their affecting commits ancestors of origin/main.
Bind the exact SceneSpec hash, requested output spelling, runtime binary hashes, release commit, production tool hashes and 100 GiB disk-reserve decision.
Validate SceneSpec and compile BuildPlan twice in memory with canonical-byte identity, but start zero Blender processes and create neither attempt nor output root.
Write an immutable self-hashed ACCEPTED or REJECTED record using exclusive creation.
compileRequirements: Write and fsync sequence-1 attempt before admission.
Reopen the accepted pushed preflight with the unchanged formal admission module and require exact SceneSpec, output spelling, release and tool bindings.
Write and fsync sequence-2 admission plus sequence-3 attempt receipt before creating the output root or starting compiler processes.
After authorization, create the output root and fsync sequence-4 formal-start before compiling the immutable BuildPlan.
Invoke the unchanged restricted compiler exactly once and retain its budget report and CompileReceipt without rewriting either.

Write one self-hashed production receipt binding the complete authorization chain, BuildPlan, PID-bearing budget report, current CompileReceipt, manifest, canonical structure and compiled .blend artifact.
On rejection, write a self-hashed failure plus receipt with scientificVerdict null, start zero Blender processes and never materialize the requested output root.
verifierRequirements: Do not import the production runner and do not trust stored verdicts.
Recompute every file and canonical self-hash, verify git ancestry and sequence ordering, and reject unbound or backup outputs.
Invoke the unchanged current CompileReceipt verifier and require PASS with exactly 19 checks.
Independently require BFS_BUDGETED_PROCESS_RESULT version 0.2.0, PASS, exact native Blender command and a positive safe-integer child.pid.
Invoke the frozen Blender artifact auditor and require embedded planHash, structureHash, manifest version and Blender build hash bindings.
Emit a self-hashed verification result and a nonzero exit status on any mismatch.

requirements: Exact preregistration, B55 parent evidence, package minimality, runtime identities, release manifest and all seven new tool hashes.
All new production/B56 paths and unchanged production dependencies are tracked-clean at one pushed tool-freeze commit.
The preferred preflight npm alias creates four accepted production preflights for B01-A/B and B02-A/B with exact output bindings.
SceneSpec suite remains 22/22 and two in-memory BuildPlan calls per run remain canonical-byte exact at the frozen plan hashes.

Negative probes for absolute/outside/symlink/existing output, dirty tool, dirty SceneSpec, unpushed release, output swap and blocked disk admission reject before Blender and without attempt/output materialization.
Projected 512 MiB write leaves at least 100 GiB free.
Attempt and formal roots remain absent before accepted preflight creation.

auditContract.independence: The B56 auditor must not import the production preflight, production runner, production receipt library, production verifier, B56 preflight or B56 runner. It may invoke the preferred verifier npm alias as an external child and must independently reopen all source and evidence bytes.
requiredAttackFamilies: package alias replacement, removal and extra package mutation
release manifest or frozen dependency hash mutation
SceneSpec hash, output spelling or preflight-evidence commit swap
absolute, outside-repository, symlink and pre-existing output paths
attempt missing, admission rejection hidden, sequence reorder and output-before-receipt
BuildPlan hash, budget report hash, native PID and current CompileReceipt mutation
production receipt self-hash, structure hash, manifest and .blend binding mutation
unexpected output, backup file, process-count, render, model, network and Docker mutation
stored verdict flip with recomputed self-hash
auditContract.verdictValidation: Outcome-neutral: derive supported versus rejected from all observed gates; a frozen tool/process exception invalidates with scientificVerdict null.

diskAdmission.cleanupObservation: Only explicitly authorized rebuildable caches were cleared. Qwen models, Blender worker images, Colima profiles and repository evidence were preserved.

decision.supportedWhen: All 27 gates pass; all four preferred production alias invocations and independent verifiers pass; the authorization chain precedes every output and compiler process; B01/B02 plan and structure identities remain frozen; and at least 48 semantic attacks are rejected.
decision.invalidated: Any frozen tool/process exception produces scientificVerdict null, preserves partial evidence and forbids same-ID repair or rerun.

nonClaims: This does not modify, repair or rerun B54-E1 or B55-E1.
This does not claim deterministic .blend container bytes.
This does not render pixels or prove cinematic image quality.
B01/B02 remain minimal compiler benchmarks, not full actor, cloth, hair, simulation or production-lighting coverage.
A local Git ancestry chain, SHA-256 receipt and supervisor PID are not signatures, cryptographic process identity or remote attestation.
Production mode requires committed and pushed trusted inputs; compile:restricted remains available for explicitly non-release development probes.
A supported result promotes an auditable compiler entry only; it does not establish the broader cinematic workflow as complete.
nextBoundary: If supported, use compile:production as the preferred release entry and separately preregister the next representative-scene coverage experiment. Any later production manifest, admission, supervisor, compiler, receipt, verifier or package-entry change must rerun this B01/B02 production regression.
